Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

change verb

make or become different

also alter, alteration, make different, become different, change one’s ways, modify

classical

Cic. Sen. 10: nec senectūs mōrēs mūtāverat

mūtō, mūtāre, mūtāvī, mūtātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive; passive mūtārī, to change, become different

change, alter

The general word. It also means to exchange one thing for another (see swap), and to change clothes.

Other words

  • commūtō, commūtāre, commūtāvī, commūtātum — change entirely

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.31: quae commūtantur fīuntque contrāria (Lewis & Short)

    Change wholly; most frequent in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • immūtō, immūtāre, immūtāvī, immūtātum — change, alter

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 214: verbōrum ōrdinem immūtā (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • erat enim in illō virō cōmitāte condīta gravitās, nec senectūs mōrēs mūtāverat

    for in that man gravity was seasoned with kindness, and old age had not changed his waysCic. Sen. 10

  • quid rīdēs? mūtātō nōmine dē tē fābula narrātur

    why are you laughing? Change the name, and the story is about youHor. S. 1.1.69–70

  • Nōn satis est dolēre, nisi mōrēs mūtāre velīs.

    Being sorry is not enough, unless you mean to change your ways.Cord. Coll. 2.39

See also change, trade, transform, become.
